expected_failure_modes: Short, unique or low-repetition responses produce no acceleration and retain policy overhead.
An identical context can precede changed content; agreement among historical continuations does not guarantee the next continuation.
Useful repeats outside the 96-token window, contexts shorter than four or single-token matches are discarded.
Copying long repeated semantic content can waste verification work after a mismatch.
GPU numerical disagreement, stop and bonus conventions, real block and rollback costs remain unresolved.
Even two agreeing prior occurrences can be confidently wrong when the same context changes its continuation or reaches EOS; an executable counterexample is preserved in shift_results/analysis.json.
Even very high acceptance may fail to amortize block or policy-executor costs.
JSON state transport can dominate policy execution for long questions or histories; this cost is host-dependent and was measured only with stdlib JSON on the local CPU.
A same-question identical public state can be either a replay or a new response; no public request ID permits reliable distinction, so the controller remains idempotent.

Concurrent requests with the same question and compatible prefixes cannot be identified from this interface. Distinct exact question strings are isolated; incompatible prefixes reset learning. Returned IDs always come from the current history.

Internal block caps or skipped callbacks followed by bonus/ordinary tokens can make continuation matches differ from true verified acceptance. Internal accepted/proposed counters describe inferred matching evidence, not host-reported acceptance or a formal metric.
Final proposals often have no later callback. Terminal censorship selectively removes some full, rejected or EOS observations; the controller discards unresolved evidence on detectable restarts.
Adaptive cooldown can remove useful opportunities and costs more CPU than stateless reuse. Synthetic distributions and hypothetical verifier costs cannot choose the actual latency winner.

historical_reuse_algorithm.state: At most 16 LRU tracks keyed by exact string questions up to 4096 characters. Valid supported nonterminal calls record a complete history up to 128 IDs, including abstention; budgets below two do not update tracks. Shortened or changed histories reset learning when observed. Unsupported questions and histories longer than 128 IDs use stateless reuse. Identical histories and budgets replay the same proposal, including cooldown abstention; changed budgets recompute without consuming another cooldown.
historical_reuse_algorithm.strategy: Match the longest 4..8-token suffix against earlier nonoverlapping occurrences in the last 96 public generated token IDs. Copy up to four following IDs only while every occurrence agrees, requiring at least two proposed tokens. Keep at most 16 question-keyed pending proposals; on the next compatible public history infer the matched prefix, shrink to horizon 2 after a mismatch, and grow from 2 to 4 after a full observed acceptance.

stochastic_boundary_research.interpretation: Shared noise does not guarantee shared logits, sampler-stage arithmetic or retained cache state. Support and log-margin conditions are sufficient only in ideal arithmetic under justified bounds. Refined possible-entrant conditions reduce conservative uncertainty, but observed pair errors do not certify future errors. Canonical replay must restore/rebuild retained state and reuse unchanged position noise.
stochastic_boundary_research.limitations: Synthetic logits/noise, deliberately noise-conditioned boundary fixtures and scalar rounding are not target distributions, GPU kernels, trusted sampler emulation, target equality, speedup or formal scores. Current-token stability does not certify subsequent cache-dependent decisions.
